rows.what the ink shows: The superscript above L is a small sideways double lobe: the right oval returns into a compressed left lobe, rather than making the single upright oval of 0.

On targeted reinspection, the tall looped l and adjoining e body are followed to their right by an additional upper wedge and a separate lower stroke turning right, down and back. Those two terminal strokes extend beyond the e return and support a final s. The following word has a distinct v entry and a low linked erra sequence, giving les verra.

The deletion line crosses the baseline, but the initial two tall angular strokes survive above it, followed by low rounded humps and a short rightward terminal stroke. The same page has an uncancelled Alors with this tall A/l opening and low ors ending immediately before the first displayed integral.

Within the alpha parentheses the e/x cluster is followed by a separate p-shaped downstroke and then s on the same writing line. The s is not raised as an exponent; several baseline letters precede it.
After the closing parenthesis there is one compact, dark, three-level curled glyph with a broad upper stroke and lower return. The space before it contains no separate oval or ascending d-stem.

The word begins with an r-like upright and curved shoulder, then has a conspicuous tall crossed t. The following low horizontal connection leads into small joined round and v-shaped humps and a short terminal e stroke, supporting retrouve despite the compression.

The glyph immediately after the raised p has a broad top stroke, a small middle turn and a descending lower curl. It is a single compact xi; there is no intervening d with its own bowl or upright stem.

Between est and la there is a small open initial curve, two extremely compressed horizontal runs separated by short marks, and a long final return rising to an angular t-like end. The medial letter loops and the initial accent cannot be separated securely even in the enlarged contrast view, so the full proposed spelling remains uncertain.

The superscript has one continuous horizontal figure-eight: exactly two adjacent enclosed eyes with a crossing waist. There is no second figure-eight and no separate oval zero. The tall descending stroke immediately to its right belongs to the closing parenthesis.

A low opening curve and raised oval/downstroke make the initial d visible at the left. A detached dot survives farther right, but the long dark cancellation bar merges nearly all subsequent letter bodies. The remaining bumps and dot do not independently identify the full proposed omaine.

Under the cancellation stroke the first letter retains its descending p stem, followed by a small round o, a short bent low stroke for s, and an elongated closing e loop. The repeated uncancelled pose immediately to the right provides local comparison for the compressed cursive word.

After W there is a cancelled parenthesized f: a small left curve, tall looped stem with a descending hooked foot and low right loop, crossed by cancellation strokes, followed by a right parenthesis. A separate clear pair of parentheses then encloses phi with a loop and long downward stem and a low overtraced two-loop g. This visible deleted argument is absent from the listed candidate.

Between the abbreviated measurable phrase and support, the very small letter consists of a dark low arched body with a separate short oblique grave stroke above it. The accent is detached from the body and is not a continuation of the neighboring tall letter.

An initial detached dot is visible above the left end and a few low loops and vertical projections survive along the word, but a thick horizontal cancellation stroke covers the bodies. The central letters and accent cannot be separated well enough to establish intégrables from their own ink.

Before disqué the struck word retains an opening curved hook at the left and several small humps and a diagonal terminal stroke, but the opaque bar joins the interior letter forms. No separate n, v, or x crossing can be distinguished reliably beneath it, so convexe remains unconfirmed.
